summary: Frontend-only bug-fix verification for the 'APK direct pour Android' download button on the Next.js marketing site (localhost:3001). All 7 test scenarios passed. The placeholder APK is served correctly (HTTP 200, 803 bytes). The store-android-btn is now an <a href download> that triggers a native browser download on both desktop and Android UA. store-ios-btn correctly shows the 'Disponible prochainement sur l'App Store' toast without triggering any download. hero-download-btn uses handleSmartDownload: on desktop and Android UA it downloads the APK, on iPhone UA it shows the App Store toast. All content routes (/legal, /blog, /prestataires, /contact, /apropos) return HTTP 200. No JS console errors were captured during any interaction.
critical_code_review_comments: DownloadButton.tsx is clean, small, well-typed and uses env-vars correctly with sensible defaults. No refactor needed.

The placeholder APK (803-byte ZIP) is fine for URL/download-plumbing verification but must be replaced by a real signed build before public release — recommend documenting this in the deployment checklist.
context_for_next_testing_agent: APK download plumbing verified end-to-end on localhost:3001. Files: /app/website/public/downloads/jokoo-latest.apk (803B ZIP placeholder), /app/website/app/components/DownloadButton.tsx (StoreButtons uses <a href download>). Playwright helpers used: page.expect_download() and browser.new_context(user_agent=...) for UA spoofing.
